title: Replication spec for "The "Rough" HAR model" - September 2026 draft
sample: Primary sample: 10 US ETFs = SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY) + 9 Select Sector SPDR Funds (XLB,XLE,XLF,XLI,XLK,XLP,XLU,XLV,XLY) which partition the S&P 500. Daily realized variance (RV) and realized quarticity (RQ) computed from TAQ data at 5-minute sampling frequency. M=78 intraday 5-min returns per 6.5-hour trading day. Secondary robustness sample: panel of 40 individual stocks listed in Table tab:stock_symbols from VOLARE database (http://volare.unime.it). Filters/cleaning: not stated beyond 5-min sampling and TAQ source. Sample sizes: roughly 3,770 trading days for ETFs; 500-obs rolling window for forecasting; 40 stocks from 2015-01-02 to 2026-01-30.
method: 1. Data construction: For each asset and day t, compute r_{t,i} i=1..M 5-min returns. RV_t = sum_{i=1}^M r_{t,i}^2. RQ_t = M/3 sum_{i=1}^M r_{t,i}^4. BPV_t = mu_1^{-2} sum_{i=1}^{M-1} |r_{t,i}||r_{t,i+1}| with mu_1=sqrt(2/pi). J_t = max(RV_t-BPV_t,0). RS_t^+ = sum r_{t,i}^2 I(r_{t,i}>0), RS_t^- = sum r_{t,i}^2 I(r_{t,i}<0). Work with y_j = log RV_j for estimation of AR/RAR/HAR/RHAR/fBm/fOU.

2. Continuous-time benchmarks: fBm y_t = sigma B^H_t with representation def-fbm; fGn autocovariance eq acf_fgn. fOU dy_t = kappa(mu-y_t)dt+sigma dB^H_t with solution and discrete exact eq fou_discrete y_{iDelta}=exp(-kappa Delta) y_{(i-1)Delta}+(1-exp(-kappa Delta))mu + eta_{iDelta}, eta_{iDelta}=sigma int_{(i-1)Delta}^{iDelta} exp(-kappa(iDelta-s)) dB^H_s, Delta=1/250 years. Estimate fBm by Whittle method of Fukasawa-Takabatake 2019; fOU by exact MLE of Wang-Xiao-Yu-Zhang 2025. SE from analytical asymptotic covariance.

3. Discrete-time “rough” models: AR: eq ar1-spec y_j = omega + rho y_{j-1}+ epsilon_j. RAR: same with epsilon_j = varepsilon_j + theta varepsilon_{j-1}. HAR: eq har-spec y_j = omega + rho1 y_{j-1}+ rho2 y_{j-1|j-5}+ rho3 y_{j-1|j-22}+ epsilon_j where y_{j-i|j-l}=1/(l-i+1) sum_{p=i}^l y_{j-p}. RHAR: HAR with epsilon_j = varepsilon_j + theta varepsilon_{j-1}. varepsilon_j ~ i.i.d. N(0,sigma^2). Estimate AR/HAR by OLS; RAR/RHAR by exact MLE via Kalman filter. SE: OLS formulas, OPG for RAR, Hessian for RHAR. HAR extensions for horse-race: HARQ RV_t = beta0+(beta1+beta1Q RQ_{t-1}^{1/2})RV_{t-1}+beta2 RV_{t-1|t-5}+beta3 RV_{t-1|t-22}+u_t; HARJ RV_t = beta0+beta1 RV_{t-1}+beta2 RV_{t-1|t-5}+beta3 RV_{t-1|t-22}+beta_j J_{t-1}+u_t; HARS RV_{t+h}=beta0+beta1^+ RS_t^+ +beta1^- RS_t^- +beta2 RV_{t|t-4}+beta3 RV_{t|t-21}+eps_{t+h}.

4. Wold approximation theory: fGn spectral density f(lambda)=2 C_H (1-cos lambda)(2pi)^{-1-2H}[zeta(1+2H,1-lambda/2pi)+zeta(1+2H,lambda/2pi)] with C_H=sigma^2(2pi)^{-1} Gamma(2H+1) sin(pi H), zeta Hurwitz. Under log f in L1 and Szego condition f admits factorization f(lambda)=sigma_eps^2/(2pi) |C(e^{-i lambda})|^2, C(z)=sum_{j>=0} c_j z^j, c0=1. Compute cepstral coefficients a_k =1/(2pi) int_{-pi}^{pi} log f(lambda) e^{-ik lambda} d lambda via FFT on fine equispaced midpoint grid wrapped to (-pi,pi] (singularity at 0 avoided). Recover Wold coefficients via recursion eq pourahmadi_recursion c_{k+1}=sum_{j=0}^k (1-j/(k+1)) a_{k+1-j} c_j. Innovation variance sigma_eps^2 =2pi exp(a0)=|h(0)|^2 2pi. Compute c_j j=0..100; report j=0..10. Approximate tail sum_{j>100} c_j^2 negligible. Share var explained by first lag = c1^2 / sum_{j=1}^{100} c_j^2. Truncate at q=1: X_t approx varepsilon_t + c1 varepsilon_{t-1}. c1 negative for H<1/2, near linear in H, range approx -1 to 0 as H 0->0.5.

5. Simulation DGP - sample paths: simulate 500 daily obs each model sigma=1, fBm/fOU H=0.2 Delta=1/250 kappa=2 mu=0 for fOU, RAR omega=0 rho=0.95 theta=-0.4, RHAR omega=0 (rho1,rho2,rho3)=(0.70,0.15,0.10) theta=-0.4 same theta for comparison.

6. Simulation - Hurst recovery: DGP1 fBm in unit-root form B^H_t=B^H_{t-1}+x_t x_t fGn; DGP2 fOU sampled at Delta=1/250 with kappa in {2,5} (additional table kappa=5), simulated on fine grid 10 sub-steps per day via AR discretization eq fou_discrete with midpoint approx of innovation integral, burn-in 500 days discarded for stationarity. Grid H in {0.1,0.2,0.3,0.4} and finer grid 0.05..0.45 for curve check. Sample sizes n in {500,4000}. 500 replications per cell. Estimate RAR/RHAR by exact MLE via Kalman filter. At each replication invert c1(.) mapping restricted to H in (0,1/2) to get implied H_imp = c1^{-1}(hat theta) then average. Exclude replications where likelihood fails to converge, at most 6 of 500 per cell. Treat boundary pile-up: re-estimate from interior start values, cap just inside invertibility boundary when no interior optimum.

7. Forecasting horse-race: horizons h =1 day, 1 week (=5 days), 1 month (=22 days). Benchmark HAR. Models: HAR,HARQ,HARJ,HARS,Log-AR,Log-RAR,Log-HAR,Log-RHAR,fBm,fOU. Fit on rolling window 500 trading days (~2 years) rolled forward 1 day, re-estimate each step. For log-models convert to level via log-normal correction hat RV_{t+h}=exp(hat y_{t+h}+ hat s_h^2/2) where hat s_h^2 model-implied forecast error variance. Insanity filter for ALL forecasts: if forecast outside [min RV, max RV] observed in estimation window replace by mean RV over that window. Losses: MSE=(hat RV_t - RV_t)^2 ; QLIKE= RV_t/hat RV_t - log(RV_t/hat RV_t)-1. Report ratio avg loss(model)/avg loss(HAR); value <1 improvement. Star notation from MCS.

8. MCS test: set M0={1..M} 10 models. Loss diff d_{ij,t}=L_{i,t}-L_{j,t}. Null H0,Ms: E d_{ij,t}=0 for all i,j in Ms. Alternative exists i,j with !=0. Statistic T_max,Ms = max studentized avg loss differential vs others. Bootstrap block length 20, 5000 replications. If not reject at level, Ms is confidence set; else eliminate worst model per Hansen-Lunde-Nason rule and iterate. MCS p-value for eliminated model e_Ms = max_{k <= s} P_{H0,Mk} where M1 superset ... superset Ms. Three stars=member of 75% set (p>0.25), two stars=90% set (p>0.10), one star=95% set (p>0.05), no star excluded. Applied per ETF/horizon/loss separately.

9. Measurement-error robustness: state-space eq logrv-noise y_j = x_j + w_j, x_j = omega + phi x_{j-1}+ v_j + theta v_{j-1}, w_j perp v_j white noise, fix sigma_w^2 =2/m =1/39 exactly (m=78) from Theorem 2.1 Fukasawa-Takabatake-Westphal asymptotic independence/normality. Estimate by MLE via Kalman filter. Testable restriction noise-only => theta=0. Report theta with 95% CI per ETF (Figure theta_noise).
